long_biography.plain_text:
Gregory Alan Pickett came to sports nutrition through product formulation and racing. With his son Michael, he acquired the Cytomax brand from a former employer and founded CytoSport in 1998. Pickett’s flavor work helped transform a niche supplement formula into Muscle Milk, whose ready-to-drink format opened a broader consumer market. The family retained control as the company scaled, then sold it to Hormel Foods.

Pickett used the same formulation experience to build Flavor Insights, a contract developer serving food and beverage companies from Benicia, California. Motorsport formed an equally persistent second career. He won the Trans-Am championship, competed across six decades and later fielded a professional sports-car team that captured consecutive American Le Mans Series titles. The business financed the racing platform; the racing programme also became a proving ground and public identity for the Muscle Milk brand.

Pickett used the same formulation experience to build Flavor Insights, a contract developer serving food and beverage companies from Benicia, California. Motorsport formed an equally persistent second career. He won the Trans-Am championship, competed across six decades and later fielded a professional sports-car team that captured consecutive American Le Mans Series titles. The business financed the racing platform; the racing programme also became a proving ground and public identity for the Muscle Milk brand.
